Re: Appeal of denial of prior authorization for cervical fusion  
Member: Reese Jennings  
Member ID: W714739496  
Reference number: POC-0A9468429E-28212  
Requested procedure: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion  
CPT: 22551  
Date of denial notice: August 16, 2026  

Dear Anthem Blue Cross Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the requested C5-C6 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The records do document substantially more than a six-week trial of conservative care, together with persistent and progressive neurologic findings.

The clinical record establishes the following:

- I have experienced progressive neck pain for approximately nine months. The pain has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, from April 1, 2026, through June 24, 2026. I completed 18 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for approximately six months, without adequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on May 16, 2026. It produced only two weeks of partial relief, followed by continuing symptoms.
- I continue to have radicular pain and numbness extending into the right thumb and index finger, with weakness.
- Examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.
- The July 22, 2026, cervical MRI shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and compression of the C6 nerve root.
- The requested surgery is directed at the documented C5-C6 structural abnormality and corresponding right C6 symptoms.

These records directly address the stated reason for denial. Conservative treatment was attempted for substantially longer than six weeks and included supervised therapy, medication, and injection treatment. The treatment did not adequately relieve the symptoms. The patient also has objective clinical findings and imaging that correlate at the same level, as well as weakness and sensory symptoms indicating neurologic involvement.

The submitted records further document the absence of several potentially relevant risk factors: there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, the BMI is 29, and the patient is a non-smoker.

I request that Anthem overturn the denial and authorize CPT 22551. If Anthem continues to rely on a medical policy or clinical review guideline, please identify the exact document, version, effective date, and specific criteria applied to this request, and provide a copy of those criteria. The publicly available materials I located do not establish which California-specific policy or proprietary clinical criteria were applied to this determination, so the appeal should be reviewed using the complete clinical record and the actual criteria relied upon by Anthem.

Please include the physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection record, MRI report, and examination findings in the review. If additional information is needed, please contact the treating surgeon, Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery.

Please reverse the denial and approve the requested cervical fusion. If the clinical reviewer believes a peer-to-peer discussion is necessary, please arrange one with Duval, MD. If the treating physician determines that delay could jeopardize neurologic function or recovery, please also process this request under Anthem’s expedited appeal procedure.

Sincerely,

Reese Jennings
